questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD mastery of multi-resource coordination, init containers, volumes, secrets, and network policies. It also validates per-namespace config management and safe log persistence.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job orchestration across a namespace
- InitContainer to install client tooling and share /tools
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for migrations and DB credentials
- PVC-backed /logs for auditability
- NetworkPolicy restricting egress to Postgres
- Status tracking in a namespace ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
spec:
  schedule: "*/12 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: migrations
            configMap:
              name: migrations-config
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client && mkdir -p /tools && cp /usr/bin/psql /tools/psql"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
          containers:
          - name: migrate
            image: migrate-base:latest
            command: ["/tools/psql","-h","$(DB_HOST)","-U","$(DB_USER)","-d","$(DB_NAME)","-f","/migrations/*.sql"]
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-credentials
            - configMapRef:
                name: db-config
            volumeMounts:
            - name: migrations
              mountPath: /migrations
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- InitContainer size vs main image size; tooling duplication
- Per-namespace migrations risk drift vs centralized control
- Secret rotation complexity; ensure timely updates
- Logging volume retention vs cost

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical CKAD design: per-namespace health tests, config-driven behavior, and restricted network access.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped Deployment
- ConfigMap-driven probe config
- Secrets for API token
- InitContainer tooling
- PVC-backed logs
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal YAML skeleton for the Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: canary-health-tester
  namespace: PLACEHOLDER
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: canary-health-tester
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
      containers:
        - name: tester
          image: curlimages/curl:8.90.0
          args: ["/bin/sh","-c","/bin/true"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 15
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: logs-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would token rotation be handled and what about refresh latency?
- What are the trade-offs of per-namespace vs central tester deployment?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a scheduled, idempotent data archival workflow using core Kubernetes primitives (CronJob, PVCs, ConfigMap, InitContainer, HTTP post, probes) with practical considerations for reliability (backoff, history limits) and operations (PDB).

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and job lifecycles
- PVC data/input and output destinations
- InitContainer usage for tooling installation
- ConfigMap-driven thresholds and defaults
- Resource requests/limits, probes, backoff, and RBAC considerations
- PodDisruptionBudget applicability to ephemeral batch workloads

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton patch (CronJob)
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-archiver
  namespace: nightly-backups
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 3
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: archiver
            image: my-registry/archiver:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
            - name: backups
              mountPath: /backups
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: "100m"
                memory: "128Mi"
              limits:
                cpu: "500m"
                memory: "256Mi"
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "/usr/local/bin/archiver.sh"]
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "test -d /data && true"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 30
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "test -f /backups/backup-*.tar.gz || true"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
              periodSeconds: 60
          volumes:
          - name: data
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: data-pvc
          - name: backups
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backups-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
        
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test behavior when backup-config DAYs_OLDER changes in-flight?
- How would you rollback a failed run and protect against partial backups?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests RBAC scoping, CronJob scheduling, and in-cluster data backup to a ConfigMap without leaking secrets.

## Key Concepts
- RBAC granularity scoped to a namespace
- CronJob scheduling and Job templates
- Reading Kubernetes events via API in-cluster
- Updating/creating a ConfigMap from a Job

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: events-backup-role
  namespace: metrics
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["events"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","update","create","patch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: events-backup-binding
  namespace: metrics
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: events-backup-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: events-backup
  namespace: metrics
spec:
  schedule: "*/2 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: events-backup-sa
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl get events -n metrics -o json | jq '.items[0:50]' > /backup/events.json; kubectl create configmap events-backup --from-file=events.json=/backup/events.json -n metrics --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: backup
            emptyDir: {}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor the ConfigMap growth and avoid hitting 1MiConfigMap limit?
- How would you rollback if the CronJob misbehaves or RBAC scope expands unintentionally?

```javascript
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: payments-egress
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.45/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

> Note: DNS-based egress restrictions are not widely supported in NetworkPolicy; use the processor’s IP in the ipBlock.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of per-namespace batch processing, using ConfigMap as data, InitContainer tooling, and a small controller to translate YAML into Kubernetes Jobs.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven runtime data
- InitContainer for kubeval
- Lightweight controller to create Jobs
- Rate limiting and idempotent applies
- checksum/config annotation for rolling restarts
- Probes and PDB for reliability
- Load testing and rollback strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: batcher
  namespace: etl
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: "<computed>"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: batcher
```

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question assesses the ability to design per-namespace tooling that leverages core Kubernetes primitives without requiring cluster-scoped operators. It validates understanding of security boundaries, namespace isolation, and storage patterns in a cloud-native context.

## Key Concepts Tested

- **Metrics API access and per-namespace RBAC**: Querying `metrics.k8s.io` requires a ClusterRoleBinding or Role with `get` permissions on `pods.metrics.k8s.io` scoped to the target namespace.
- **ConfigMap-driven configuration**: Externalizing the aggregation window enables runtime adjustments without redeploying.
- **Security hardening**: NetworkPolicy, least-privilege ServiceAccounts, and Secret management demonstrate defense-in-depth thinking.
- **Operational concerns**: PVCs for logs, health probes, and init containers address real-world reliability requirements.

## Common Pitfalls

- Forgetting that `metrics.k8s.io` is a custom API group requiring proper RBAC—not included in default `view`/`edit` ClusterRoles.
- Overly permissive NetworkPolicies that allow all egress instead of targeting specific endpoints.
- Storing secrets as plain environment variables instead of referencing them from a Secret resource.

## Extensions

- Add a CronJob wrapper to schedule aggregation runs rather than running continuously.
- Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures when posting to the portal.
- Consider adding Prometheus metrics to the aggregator itself for observability of the observability tool.

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- CronJob per-namespace scheduling
- ConfigMap/Secret usage for config and credentials
- InitContainer provisioning of benchmarking tools
- Logs to PVC and metrics to ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: bench-endpoint
  namespace: {NAMESPACE}
spec:
  schedule: "*/15 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache wrk && sleep 1"]
          containers:
            - name: bench
              image: appropriate/curl
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "wrk -t2 -c50 -d30s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $BENCH_TOKEN\" $BENCH_ENDPOINT || true"]
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: bench-config
              env:
                - name: BENCH_ENDPOINT
                  valueFrom:
                    configMapKeyRef:
                      name: bench-config
                      key: endpoint
                - name: BENCH_TOKEN
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: bench-secret
                      key: token
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: bench-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Why This Is Asked

- ConfigMap/Secret mounts

```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: stock-service
  namespace: inventory
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-db
        image: postgres:15
        command:
        - bash
        - -lc
        - until pg_isready -h postgresql.inventory.svc -p 5432; do sleep 2; done; psql -h postgresql.inventory.svc -U dbuser -d inventory -f /seed/init.sql
        env:
        - name: PGPASSWORD

        - name: seed-files

      - name: stock-service
        image: my-reg/stock-service:latest
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:

        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: seed-files
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical batch-job composition: init tooling, config-driven scripts, and safe cleanup. 

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Job TTL, backoff, and completion semantics
- InitContainers alongside main containers
- ConfigMap and Secret mounts; env from Secret
- Resource requests/limits; idempotence

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
  namespace: migrate
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
  backoffLimit: 3
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client"]
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: postgres:15
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
          env:
            - name: PGHOST
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: host
          command: ["psql","-h","$(PGHOST)","-U","$(POSTGRES_USER)","-d","migration_db","-f","/migrate/scripts/migrate.sql"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: migrate-scripts
              mountPath: /migrate/scripts
      volumes:
        - name: migrate-scripts
          configMap:
            name: migrate-scripts
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate idempotence for repeated runs?
- How would you rollback if migration fails after partial progress?
